taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-22, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 177.3 | 1.37 | 1.37
2 | 706.0 | 5.88 | 7.25
3 | 3320.1 | 2.09 | 9.34
4 | 3433.8 | 1.21 | 10.55
5 | 794.3 | 10.44 | 20.99
6 | 9531.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-22, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-22 (Survey Area T)**

Station T-22 exhibits a 6-layer geoelectric profile:
- **Layer 1:** 177.3 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 1.37 m (depth to base 1.37 m)
- **Layer 2:** 706.0 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 5.88 m (depth to base 7.25 m)
- **Layer 3:** 3320.1 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 2.09 m (depth to base 9.34 m)
- **Layer 4:** 3433.8 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 1.21 m (depth to base 10.55 m)
- **Layer 5:** 794.3 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 10.44 m (depth to base 20.99 m; target zone)
- **Layer 6:** 9531.9 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (resistive basement)

Sequential analysis of the three-layer sets yields:
- 1-2-3: $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$ (A)
- 2-3-4: $r_2 < r_3 < r_4$ (A)
- 3-4-5: $r_3 < r_4 > r_5$ (K)
- 4-5-6: $r_4 > r_5 < r_6$ (H)

The resulting curve type is **AAKH**, fully consistent with the classification on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "AAKH", "label_issue_flagged": false}
